name: SysAdminSuite Reversible Printer Mapping & Audit
sprintRole: Map, unmap, or audit shared Windows printers through the canonical SysAdminSuite technician workflow with network-aware preflight, system-wide state verification, explicit reversible intent, collision handling, and per-target evidence instead of ad hoc GUI or one-off scripts
useWhen: One or many managed PCs need a shared printer queue mapped, removed, audited, or reconciled and technicians need a portable short-command workflow that works across supported network postures without blindly remapping or mutating unrelated trust/DNS/firewall/GPO state.
inspectFirst: Current SysAdminSuite printer command/wrapper and printer evidence contract; target hostname resolution; approved network posture; print server and queue identity; current machine-wide printer state; existing port/queue/name collisions; supported map/unmap mechanism; WhatIf/preview and confirmation semantics; retry/serialization policy; and current restrictions on direct-IP, trust, DNS/firewall, GPO, per-user fallback, and test-page actions.
expectedOutput: A resolved printer plan and reversible receipt for each target/queue: network/reachability result, canonical queue identity, current state, intended MAP/UNMAP/AUDIT action, collision decision, explicit confirmation, machine-wide post-state, paired undo information, failure class, and evidence pointer. Batch runs retain per-host/per-queue detail plus a rollup.
nextStep: After the read-only plan is green and the requested action is explicitly confirmed at the level the canonical SAS workflow requires, execute the bounded map/unmap owner, verify machine-wide post-state, and retain the exact undo/evidence pointer; blocked network or queue-resolution cases remain unmutated.
proofGate: No mapping occurs before target/network/queue resolution and plan visibility; MAP and UNMAP are paired and state-aware; repeated runs do not blindly duplicate work; system-wide state is verified using the repository's canonical reader; collisions are explicit; unsupported direct-IP or per-user fallbacks are not invented; and trust, DNS, firewall, GPO, or test-page mutation is outside this prompt unless a separate authorized owner explicitly governs it.
copyContent:
MAP, UNMAP, OR AUDIT WINDOWS PRINTERS THROUGH SYSADMINSUITE AS A REVERSIBLE FIELD WORKFLOW. DO NOT BLINDLY REMAP, FALL BACK TO A DIFFERENT SECURITY/NETWORK MODEL, OR TURN A QUEUE PROBLEM INTO TRUST/DNS/FIREWALL/GPO MUTATION.

Repo/product: SysAdminSuite or resolve the active SAS repository from context.
Targets: xyz_one_or_many_managed_windows_hosts
Printer source: xyz_print_server_and_queue_or_supported_inventory
Requested action: MAP | UNMAP | AUDIT

MISSION
Give technicians a short, repeatable, portable printer workflow that resolves the network and queue first, shows the intended change, performs only the requested machine-wide action, and leaves enough evidence to prove or undo it.

1. USE THE CANONICAL SAS PRINTER OWNER
Read current printer commands/wrappers, target resolver, network gate, state reader, evidence paths, batch schema, and map/unmap implementation. Do not replace repository-owned printer logic with a long local PowerShell snippet merely because it is convenient in the current shell.

2. RESOLVE TARGET + NETWORK + QUEUE
Confirm each endpoint identity and an approved network path to the target and print infrastructure. Resolve the canonical print server/queue rather than guessing from display names. A network mismatch is a distinct blocker; do not call the printer offline merely because the current technician machine cannot reach it.

3. READ CURRENT MACHINE-WIDE STATE
Audit the existing printer/connection/port state at the supported machine-wide level. Record whether the requested queue is absent, already mapped, mapped differently, conflicted by name/port, or unknown. Do not use a per-user fallback when the canonical workflow requires system-wide state.

4. SHOW THE PLAN BEFORE MUTATION
For each target/queue, display current state -> requested action -> expected post-state -> collision decision -> owning command. Preserve canonical WhatIf/preview behavior and explicit MAP/UNMAP confirmation when required. A large batch does not waive confirmation or plan visibility.

5. MAP / UNMAP REVERSIBLY
Use the repository-authorized system-wide mechanism and its paired inverse. MAP must have a state-derived UNMAP/undo path; UNMAP must identify exactly which machine-wide mapping is being removed. Skip already-compliant state only after the canonical reader proves it. Serialize target changes when the SAS implementation requires serialization.

6. DO NOT INVENT NETWORK OR SECURITY FALLBACKS
Do not mutate trust, DNS, firewall, GPO, VPN, routing, or directory policy to make printer mapping work. Do not use direct-IP mapping, per-user mapping, or print-test-page actions when current repository/operator policy forbids them. If a separately authorized canonical owner explicitly permits a different transport, route to that owner rather than silently changing this prompt's contract.

7. VERIFY POST-STATE
Re-read machine-wide printer state and verify the exact queue mapping/removal. Record evidence per target/queue, including collision disposition and undo information. A command exit code without state verification is not closure.

8. BATCH SAFELY
For many PCs and queues, consume the supported batch inventory, preserve a resolved plan, keep per-host/per-queue receipts, and emit a rollup that separates success, already-compliant, blocked, hard failure, and unknown. Do not lose individual failures inside an aggregate green count.

FIELD UX
Prefer clickable/short technician entrypoints with easy server/queue inputs and safe examples sourced from repository docs; do not hard-code private production infrastructure into reusable public prompt text.

DELIVER
Resolved plan, per-target/queue pre-state, action/confirmation, post-state, undo path, evidence pointer, blocked/failing items, batch rollup when relevant, proof ceiling, and exact next safe action.
